speaker_role: test-prep/consultancy marketer (founder of College Shortcuts, self-described 18-20 years in admissions space)
commercial_incentive: Heavy sales pitch throughout for College Shortcuts tutoring, mentorship, and application packages; repeated calls to schedule paid consultation calls
key_insights: Distinguishes test-optional (student chooses whether to submit scores, but submitted scores are still considered) from test-blind (scores are not considered even if sent)
Claims several highly selective schools have been reinstating SAT/ACT requirements after years of test-optional policies adopted during the pandemic
Argues going test-optional does not make admission easier because colleges then weight transcript rigor, essays, and interviews more heavily
Recommends deciding whether to submit scores on a school-by-school basis by comparing your score to each college's middle-50% range rather than using one blanket strategy
Recommends SAT/ACT prep start in 10th grade and finish by summer before 11th grade, citing junior year as the hardest year to add heavy test prep on top of everything else
States applicants can submit test scores to some colleges on the Common App while applying test-optional to others
Lists common test-optional myths: that scores don't matter at all, that no one submits scores anymore, and that going test-optional automatically improves chances
Claims interviews factor into 80-90% of admit decisions at schools that use them (unsupported figure)
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker claims interviews factor into 80%-90% of admit decisions where used (unsupported)
Speaker's own Rice University's SAT middle range cited as roughly 1530-1580
Speaker recounts a client's SAT rising from about 1250 to the 1500s after 20-30 hours of one-on-one tutoring
Speaker says a bachelor's degree can add up to seven figures in lifetime earnings versus a high school diploma (unsupported)
Speaker states in-state college costs range roughly $25,000-$80,000/year and private school costs $300,000-$350,000+ total (unsupported/unsourced)
notable_or_distinctive: Explains a workable tactical nuance -- submitting scores to some colleges but not others within the same Common App cycle -- that is less commonly discussed than the basic test-optional/test-blind distinction.
reliability_notes: This is a livestreamed sales webinar for a paid admissions consultancy; nearly all specific numbers (interview weight, tuition costs, lifetime earnings) are asserted without evidence and should be treated skeptically; heavy promotional framing throughout.
